title: How to file an insurance claim
content: To file a claim with ShieldGuard Insurance: (1) Call 1-800-SHIELD (available 24/7) for immediate assistance, especially for accidents or emergencies. (2) File online at shieldguard.com/claims by logging into your account and selecting 'File a Claim.' (3) Use the ShieldGuard mobile app under Claims > File New Claim. You will need your policy number, date and time of the incident, a description of what happened, photos of damage (if applicable), a police report number (for auto accidents or theft), and contact information for any other parties involved. A claims adjuster will be assigned within 24 hours and will contact you to schedule an inspection or gather additional information. Keep all receipts for expenses related to the claim (rental car, temporary repairs, hotel stays).

title: Claim timeline and process
content: After filing a ShieldGuard claim, here is the typical timeline: Within 24 hours, a claims adjuster is assigned and contacts you. Within 3-5 business days, the adjuster inspects the damage (in-person or via photos you submit through the app). Within 7-10 business days of inspection, you receive the adjuster's estimate and settlement offer. If you accept, payment is issued within 3-5 business days via check or direct deposit to your bank account. Complex claims (total loss, liability disputes, bodily injury) may take 30-90 days. You can check your claim status anytime at shieldguard.com/claims or in the mobile app. If you disagree with the settlement offer, you can request a re-inspection or escalate to a claims supervisor by calling 1-800-SHIELD.

title: What to do after a car accident
content: After a car accident, follow these steps: (1) Check for injuries and call 911 if anyone is hurt. (2) Move to a safe location if possible and turn on hazard lights. (3) Exchange information with the other driver: name, phone number, insurance company and policy number, driver's license number, license plate number, and vehicle make/model. (4) Take photos of all vehicle damage, the accident scene, traffic signs, and road conditions. (5) File a police report — many insurance claims require one, especially if there are injuries or significant damage. (6) Contact ShieldGuard at 1-800-SHIELD to report the accident and start your claim. (7) Do not admit fault or sign any documents from the other party's insurance company. (8) Seek medical attention even if you feel fine — some injuries take time to appear.

title: Documentation needed for claims
content: Documents commonly needed when filing a ShieldGuard claim: For auto claims: police report, photos of damage to all vehicles, the other driver's insurance information, medical records and bills (if injured), repair estimates from a licensed shop, and rental car receipts. For homeowners claims: photos or video of damage, receipts or proof of value for damaged items, contractor repair estimates, and the police report (for theft or vandalism). For life insurance claims: certified death certificate, completed claim form (available at shieldguard.com/forms), policy number, and the beneficiary's identification and banking information for direct deposit. All documents can be uploaded through the ShieldGuard mobile app or mailed to the Claims Department at PO Box 5500, Hartford, CT 06102.

title: Policy renewal process
content: ShieldGuard policies renew automatically at the end of each policy term (6 months for auto, 12 months for homeowners and renters). You will receive a renewal notice 30 days before your policy expires, detailing any changes to coverage or premium. If your premium increased, the notice explains the reason (e.g., claims history, rate adjustment, coverage change). To make changes before renewal, contact your agent or call 1-800-SHIELD at least 15 days before the renewal date. If you do not want to renew, notify ShieldGuard in writing or by phone before the renewal date to avoid being charged. Lapsed policies may require a new application and could result in higher rates. Continuous coverage with no gaps is important for maintaining favorable rates.

title: Premium payment options
content: ShieldGuard offers multiple ways to pay your premium: (1) Automatic payment (autopay) via bank account (ACH) or credit/debit card — set up at shieldguard.com/billing or by calling 1-800-SHIELD. Autopay customers receive a $3/month paperless discount. (2) Online one-time payment at shieldguard.com/pay-now using a bank account, credit card, or debit card. (3) Mobile app payment under Billing > Make a Payment. (4) Pay by phone at 1-800-SHIELD (automated system available 24/7). (5) Mail a check or money order payable to ShieldGuard Insurance, PO Box 5510, Hartford, CT 06102 — include your policy number on the check. (6) In-person at any ShieldGuard agent office. Payment frequency options: monthly, quarterly, semi-annual, or annual. Paying annually saves approximately 5% compared to monthly payments.

title: Policy cancellation
content: To cancel your ShieldGuard policy: Call 1-800-SHIELD or contact your local agent. You can also submit a written cancellation request to cancellations@shieldguard.com. Include your policy number, desired cancellation date, and reason. Cancellation can be effective immediately or on a future date. If you cancel mid-term, you may receive a pro-rated refund of your unused premium (minus any short-rate penalty if applicable). If ShieldGuard cancels your policy (for non-payment, fraud, or material misrepresentation), you will receive a written notice at least 30 days in advance for non-payment or 60 days for other reasons. A lapse in insurance coverage may be reported to your state DMV and could result in license suspension or fines depending on your state's requirements.

title: Adding a driver to your auto policy
content: To add a driver to your ShieldGuard auto policy, call 1-800-SHIELD or log in to shieldguard.com/my-policy and select 'Add Driver.' You will need the new driver's full legal name, date of birth, driver's license number and state, and driving history (any accidents or violations in the past 5 years). Adding a driver may change your premium depending on their age, driving record, and experience. Household members of driving age who have access to your vehicles generally must be listed on your policy, either as a covered driver or as an excluded driver. Excluded drivers are not covered if they operate your vehicle. Changes take effect on the date requested and your premium is adjusted pro-rata.

title: Coverage types explained: Liability
content: Liability coverage pays for injuries and property damage you cause to others in an at-fault accident. It has two components: Bodily Injury Liability (BI) covers medical expenses, lost wages, and legal costs for the other party, up to your policy limits. Property Damage Liability (PD) covers repair or replacement of the other party's vehicle or property. Liability coverage does NOT cover your own injuries or vehicle damage. Limits are expressed as three numbers, e.g., 100/300/100, meaning $100,000 per person for BI, $300,000 per accident for BI, and $100,000 for PD. Most states require minimum liability coverage to legally drive. ShieldGuard recommends at least 100/300/100 for adequate protection. Your specific coverage limits are listed on your declarations page.

title: Coverage types explained: Collision
content: Collision coverage pays to repair or replace your vehicle if it is damaged in a collision with another vehicle or object (e.g., a guardrail, tree, or pole), regardless of who is at fault. Collision coverage is subject to your deductible — you pay the deductible amount, and ShieldGuard pays the rest up to the actual cash value (ACV) of your vehicle. Common deductible amounts are $250, $500, and $1,000. Choosing a higher deductible lowers your premium but increases your out-of-pocket cost when you file a claim. Collision coverage is optional unless your vehicle is financed or leased, in which case your lender typically requires it. If your vehicle is totaled (repair cost exceeds ACV), ShieldGuard pays the ACV minus your deductible.

title: Coverage types explained: Comprehensive
content: Comprehensive coverage (sometimes called 'other than collision') covers damage to your vehicle from events that are not collisions. This includes theft, vandalism, fire, natural disasters (hail, flood, earthquake), falling objects (tree branches, debris), animal strikes (deer), glass breakage, and civil disturbances. Like collision, comprehensive is subject to a deductible. Comprehensive claims generally do not increase your premium (unlike at-fault collision claims). Comprehensive coverage is optional unless your vehicle is financed or leased. Glass-only claims (windshield repair or replacement) may have a $0 deductible depending on your state and policy. Comprehensive coverage pays up to the actual cash value of your vehicle.

title: Coverage types explained: Uninsured/Underinsured motorist
content: Uninsured Motorist (UM) coverage protects you if you are hit by a driver who has no insurance. Underinsured Motorist (UIM) coverage applies when the at-fault driver's insurance is not enough to cover your damages. UM/UIM coverage pays for your medical expenses, lost wages, and pain and suffering. Some states also offer Uninsured Motorist Property Damage (UMPD) for vehicle repairs. UM/UIM limits typically match your liability limits. This coverage is required in many states. It also covers you as a pedestrian hit by an uninsured driver or in a hit-and-run accident where the other driver cannot be identified. ShieldGuard strongly recommends UM/UIM coverage, as an estimated 13% of drivers nationally are uninsured.

title: Deductible explanation
content: A deductible is the amount you pay out of pocket before ShieldGuard begins paying on a claim. For example, if you have a $500 deductible and $3,000 in damage, you pay $500 and ShieldGuard pays $2,500. Deductibles apply to collision, comprehensive, and homeowners claims. Liability claims do not have a deductible. Choosing a higher deductible lowers your premium — a $1,000 deductible can save 15-25% compared to a $250 deductible. Choose a deductible you can comfortably afford in case of a claim. You can have different deductibles for collision and comprehensive on the same policy. The deductible is per-claim, not per-year. If you are not at fault and the other driver's insurance pays, you may recover your deductible from them.

title: Rental car coverage
content: ShieldGuard's Rental Reimbursement coverage pays for a rental car while your vehicle is being repaired after a covered claim. The coverage limit is typically $30/day for up to 30 days ($900 maximum), though higher limits are available. This coverage is optional and adds approximately $2-4/month to your premium. Without rental reimbursement coverage, you are responsible for rental car costs during repairs. When using this coverage, rent from a ShieldGuard preferred partner (Enterprise, Hertz, or National) for direct billing — otherwise, you pay upfront and submit receipts for reimbursement. Rental coverage does NOT apply if your vehicle is in for routine maintenance or mechanical breakdown; it only applies after a covered insurance claim.

title: SR-22 filing
content: An SR-22 is a certificate of financial responsibility that your state DMV may require after certain violations (DUI/DWI, driving without insurance, too many points on your license, or at-fault accidents while uninsured). ShieldGuard can file an SR-22 electronically with your state on your behalf for a one-time filing fee of $25. The SR-22 is attached to your auto insurance policy and verifies that you carry at least the state-required minimum coverage. If your policy lapses or is cancelled, ShieldGuard is required to notify your state, which may result in license suspension. SR-22 requirements typically last 3 years but vary by state and violation. Your premium will likely be higher while an SR-22 is required. Contact your agent or call 1-800-SHIELD to request an SR-22 filing.

title: Multi-policy discount
content: ShieldGuard offers a multi-policy (bundle) discount when you carry two or more policies with us. Common bundles: Auto + Homeowners saves up to 15% on both policies. Auto + Renters saves up to 10%. Auto + Life saves up to 8%. Three or more policies save up to 20%. The discount is applied automatically when policies are linked under the same account. To bundle, contact your agent or call 1-800-SHIELD. Bundled policies also simplify your billing with a single monthly payment and one point of contact for all your insurance needs. The bundle discount is one of the largest savings opportunities available and can be combined with other eligible discounts.

title: Good driver discount
content: ShieldGuard rewards safe drivers with the Good Driver Discount: up to 20% off your auto insurance premium if you have a clean driving record for the past 5 years (no at-fault accidents, no moving violations, no DUI/DWI). The discount is verified through your motor vehicle report (MVR) at policy inception and renewal. If you receive a violation or have an at-fault accident during your policy term, the discount will be removed at your next renewal. New customers receive the discount if their MVR is clean at the time of application. The Good Driver Discount can be combined with other discounts (multi-policy, good student, defensive driving).

title: Student discount
content: ShieldGuard offers two student-related auto insurance discounts. The Good Student Discount provides up to 15% off for full-time students under age 25 who maintain a B average (3.0 GPA) or higher. Proof required: a recent report card, transcript, or letter from the school. The Distant Student Discount provides up to 10% off if a listed driver under 25 is attending school more than 100 miles from home and does not have a vehicle at school. This reflects the reduced driving risk while they are away. Both discounts can be combined with other eligible discounts. Notify your agent when your student graduates or leaves school, as the discount may no longer apply.

title: Home inventory for homeowners insurance
content: A home inventory documents your personal belongings and their value, making the claims process faster and more accurate after a loss (fire, theft, natural disaster). To create a home inventory: go room by room and photograph or video each item. Record the item description, estimated value, purchase date, and serial numbers for electronics. Store receipts and appraisals for high-value items (jewelry, art, collectibles). Use the ShieldGuard mobile app's Home Inventory tool (under Policy > Home Inventory) to catalog items with photos and estimated values — the data is stored securely in the cloud. Update your inventory annually or after major purchases. Items exceeding $2,500 in value (jewelry, fine art, collectibles) may need a scheduled personal property endorsement for full coverage.

title: Flood insurance
content: Standard homeowners insurance does NOT cover flood damage. If your home is in a flood-prone area (or even if it is not — 25% of flood claims come from low-risk areas), you need a separate flood insurance policy. ShieldGuard offers flood insurance through the National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP) and through private flood insurers for higher coverage limits. NFIP policies cover up to $250,000 for the dwelling and $100,000 for contents. Private flood policies can offer higher limits and additional coverages. There is a 30-day waiting period before flood insurance takes effect (no last-minute purchases before a storm). Premiums depend on your flood zone, elevation, and building characteristics. Contact your ShieldGuard agent for a flood risk assessment and quote.

title: Umbrella policy
content: A ShieldGuard umbrella policy provides extra liability coverage beyond the limits of your auto and homeowners policies. If a lawsuit exceeds your standard policy limits, the umbrella policy covers the excess amount plus legal defense costs. Coverage starts at $1 million in increments of $1 million, up to $5 million. Premiums are affordable: approximately $150-$300/year for the first $1 million. To qualify, you typically need underlying auto liability limits of at least 250/500/100 and homeowners liability of at least $300,000. An umbrella policy also covers claims not covered by standard policies, such as libel, slander, and false imprisonment. It protects your assets (home, savings, investments) from being seized in a large lawsuit.

title: Life insurance types
content: ShieldGuard offers three types of life insurance: (1) Term Life provides coverage for a specific period (10, 20, or 30 years) at a fixed premium. If you pass away during the term, your beneficiaries receive the death benefit. If the term expires, coverage ends with no cash value. Term life is the most affordable option and ideal for covering a mortgage or supporting children until they are independent. (2) Whole Life provides lifelong coverage with a fixed premium and builds cash value over time that you can borrow against. Premiums are significantly higher than term but never increase. (3) Universal Life offers flexible premiums and death benefits. You can adjust your premium payments and coverage amount as your needs change. It also builds cash value based on current interest rates. All policies require a health questionnaire; some may require a medical exam.

title: Beneficiary changes
content: To change the beneficiary on your ShieldGuard life insurance policy: (1) Log in at shieldguard.com/my-policy and select your life insurance policy, then 'Change Beneficiary.' (2) Call 1-800-SHIELD and request a beneficiary change form. (3) Visit your local ShieldGuard agent. You will need the new beneficiary's full legal name, date of birth, Social Security number, and relationship to you. You can name multiple beneficiaries and specify percentage allocations (e.g., 50% to spouse, 25% to each child). You should also name a contingent (backup) beneficiary in case the primary beneficiary predeceases you. Beneficiary changes take effect when processed by ShieldGuard (typically 5-7 business days). Review your beneficiaries after major life events: marriage, divorce, birth of a child, or death of a beneficiary.

title: Policy transfer
content: If you are switching to ShieldGuard from another insurance company, the process is straightforward: (1) Get a quote from ShieldGuard online, by phone, or through an agent. (2) Choose your coverage and start date — set the start date to match your current policy's expiration date to avoid a coverage gap. (3) Once your ShieldGuard policy is active, cancel your old policy with your previous insurer (not before). (4) If switching auto insurance mid-term, you may receive a pro-rated refund from your previous insurer. (5) ShieldGuard's Switcher Credit offers a one-time $50 credit for customers who transfer an active policy from a competitor. Your claims history transfers with you (most insurers share claims data through the CLUE database), so prior claims may affect your ShieldGuard premium. Contact 1-800-SHIELD for a seamless transfer.

title: Proof of insurance
content: ShieldGuard provides proof of insurance (also called an insurance card or declarations page) in several formats: (1) Digital insurance card in the ShieldGuard mobile app — always up to date and accepted in all 50 states. (2) Printable insurance card available at shieldguard.com/my-policy. (3) Physical cards are mailed with your policy documents at inception and each renewal. If you need immediate proof (e.g., for a vehicle purchase or court requirement), call 1-800-SHIELD or your agent to have proof of insurance faxed or emailed to the requesting party. For real estate transactions, your agent can issue a Certificate of Insurance for your homeowners policy. If your policy has lapsed, proof of insurance will not be available until coverage is reinstated and any outstanding balance is paid.

title: Gap insurance
content: Gap insurance (Guaranteed Asset Protection) covers the difference between what you owe on your car loan or lease and the car's actual cash value (ACV) if it is totaled or stolen. For example, if your car is totaled and the ACV is $18,000 but you owe $22,000 on your loan, gap insurance pays the $4,000 difference so you are not stuck paying for a car you no longer have. Gap insurance is especially important for new vehicles (which depreciate quickly), long loan terms (60-72 months), and low or zero down payments. ShieldGuard offers gap coverage as an endorsement to your auto policy for approximately $20-40/year — significantly cheaper than gap insurance from a dealership. Gap coverage can be added at any time during your policy term.

title: Diminished value claims
content: Diminished value is the loss in your vehicle's market value after it has been in an accident and repaired. Even with a perfect repair, a vehicle with an accident history is worth less than an identical vehicle with no accident history. In many states, you can file a diminished value claim against the at-fault driver's insurance company (not your own). ShieldGuard can help you understand the process: (1) Obtain a diminished value appraisal from an independent appraiser (typically $150-$300). (2) Submit the appraisal and a demand letter to the at-fault driver's insurer. (3) Negotiate the settlement. Diminished value claims typically recover 10-25% of the vehicle's pre-accident value. Note: You generally cannot file a diminished value claim against your own insurer in most states. Contact your ShieldGuard agent for state-specific guidance.
